newsitem.title: BRAZIL: CSN says Gencor may join group for CVRD bid.
newsitem.headline: CSN says Gencor may join group for CVRD bid.

text.p: South African mining company Gencor Ltd may join the consortium led by Brazilian steelmaker CSN to bid at the privatization auction of Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), the consortium leader said.
Benjamin Steinbruch, president of CSN's Board of Directors, told reporters Gencor has not prequalified for the auction, but it still may participate.

He said Gencor could join the group by investing in a fund called "Fundo Brasil" which will be created post-privatization to allow individuals and companies, including small and medium-sized firms, to gain a stake in the special purpose company which will administer the CVRD voting stake after the auction.

Steinbruch said the consortium, named Valepar, basically is made up of CSN, four local pension funds, Opportunity Asset Management, U.S. NationsBank and the "Fundo Brasil". But more investors may join the group, he added.
He also said NationsBank will invest $1.5 billion, of which $1.2 billion to finance the CSN stake and $300 million as a full member of the consortium.
Steinbruch said other members of the consortium have not decided yet how much they would invest, but he noted the group has enough cash to buy the CVRD strategic stake.
The CSN chairman responded to criticism that CSN would have a leading position in the steel sector if it wins control of CVRD.
Newspapers have said that if CSN wins it would gain a seat on the administrative councils of four steel firms, including its main competitor, Usiminas, because CVRD has stakes in all those companies.
"I do not see how minority stakes in the steel sector indicates concentration," he said.

The CSN-led group is one of the two consortia registered with the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange to bid at the auction. The other consortium is led by Brazil's largest private conglomerate Grupo Votorantim.

A maximum 45 percent voting stake in CVRD had been due to be auctioned off Tuesday, but the government could not hold the auction due to a number of court injunctions against the firm's privatization. ((-- Fatima Cristina, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5511 2485412))
